transcript:
>> This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
Alaska Democratic Senator-elect Mary Peltola is thanking her supporters.
She posted a social media video shortly after the Associated Press called her Senate race.
>> Thank you, Alaska.
We did it.
>> From ADAC to Metlakatla to Utkiyavik, you have made your voices heard.
And it's clear that the status quo in DC cannot go on any longer.
>> Peltola's victory over Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan added Democrats a ninth GOP-held seat.
The last time Democrats picked up more than nine Senate seats in a midterm election was in 1958
during Republican Dwight Eisenhower's second term.
>> The FAA says it will temporarily stop using the types of routers involved in that technical
meltdown that caused a nationwide ground stop last week.
NPR's Joe Hernandez reports that transportation officials are still investigating what went
wrong.
>> The government contractor, L3Harris, was installing the router at a site in Arkansas
just before the technical disruptions began.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said 68 of these routers had been installed previously
without incident.
>> This is the one that started to behave this way.
So we thought it's only prudent to pause the use of these routers.
>> L3Harris sent the routers involved in Friday's incident to its lab in Florida, where officials
with the FAA and the FBI are also on site.
Duffy says there's no indication the malfunction was the result of a cyber attack, but that
the investigation is ongoing.
Joe Hernandez, NPR News.
>> A couple more tech outages Tuesday.
Apple says Apple Music, the company's App Store and Apple Care suffered full outages
and that its iCloud sign-in interface also had issues and Marriott, the nation's largest
hotel operator, says it has resolved an issue that affected the ability to sign in on its
website and the Marriott Bomboy app.
41-year-old Andrew Kozak pleaded not guilty in federal court Tuesday on two counts of
making a threat involving explosives and making that threat over email.
Kozak allegedly sent an email to Bioerger Renewables saying there were bombs inside
a facility in Peoria, Illinois, the FBI, says agents found an explosive device inside a
few hours later, Ryan Denham, a member of the WCDU reports.
>> A LinkedIn profile under Kozak's name suggests he worked at the plant as a trainee.
US attorney for Central Illinois, Gregory Gilmore, says they identified Kozak as a suspect
early on.
>> Quick action was taken.
All hands on deck and agents working 24/7, including prosecutors at full court press.
>> Officials say the plant contains ethanol and other highly combustible chemicals.
Police ordered an evacuation of 2,500 homes and businesses that lasted 18 hours as authorities
searched inside for other bombs.
No others were found.
Making threats involving explosives is a federal felony, carrying a potential sentence of up
to 10 years.
>> You're listening to NPR News.
>> Waymo has temporarily stopped freeway operations of its driverless cars nationwide after the
California DMV restricted the company's freeway use over safety concerns.
From member station KQED, Azul Dahlstrom-Eckman reports.
>> The order's been in effect since last week.
The California DMV says Waymo's freeway operations posed a quote, imminent hazard to public safety.
That's after several recent incidents, including one where three Waymo robo-taxis entered an
active construction closure on a freeway in the San Francisco Bay Area.
In a statement, Waymo said it halted freeway operations in other markets, like in Phoenix,
Arizona and Los Angeles, while its vehicles continue to operate on surface streets.
The DMV's order will be in place until Waymo provides evidence that it's corrected the
issue.
>> For NPR News, I'm Azul Dahlstrom-Eckman in San Francisco.
>> Congress has agreed to mandate that civilian aircraft carry systems that help pilots locate
nearby planes.
Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell announced the agreement Tuesday.
Lawmakers have been working on a compromise bill to address recommendations from the National
Transportation Safety Board following a deadly mid-air collision last year involving an American
Airlines flight and an Army Black Hawk helicopter.
>> The markets in Asia mixed in Wednesday trading, the markets in Japan, South Korea
and Taiwan are advancing down in Shanghai and Hong Kong after losses on Wall Street.
All three major US stock markets fell Tuesday, weighed down by artificial intelligence losses.
I'm Giles Snyder.

topics.text: Alaska Democrat Mary Peltola wins Senate race over Republican Dan Sullivan, thanks supporters
FAA pauses use of L3Harris routers after technical meltdown caused nationwide ground stop
Apple Music, App Store, iCloud and Marriott sign-in suffer outages on Tuesday
Andrew Kozak pleads not guilty to federal explosives threat charges over Peoria, Illinois plant
Waymo halts freeway driverless operations nationwide after California DMV safety restriction
Congress agrees to mandate collision-avoidance systems on civilian aircraft after DCA crash
Asian markets mixed Wednesday after US stock markets fall Tuesday on AI losses
